snippet.title: Seong-Jin Cho: Rachmaninoff’s Rhapsody on a Theme of Paganini, Op. 43 Var.18(20251203 Carnegie Hall)
snippet.description:
20251203 Carnegie Hall Presents Pittsburgh Symphony Orchestra
Stern Auditorium / Perelman Stage, Carnegie Hall, NY

Piano: Seong-Jin Cho
Pittsburgh Symphony Orchestra
Conductor : Manfred Honeck

Pianist Seong-Jin Cho joins the Pittsburgh Symphony Orchestra and conductor Manfred Honeck in a performance of Rachmaninoff’s Rhapsody on a Theme of Paganini. 

A virtuosic set of 24 variations inspired by the last of Niccolò Paganini’s 24 Caprices for Solo Violin, Rhapsody on a Theme of Paganini received its New York premiere at Carnegie Hall in 1934 with the composer as soloist alongside the New York Philharmonic led by Bruno Walter.

The swooning melody of Variation 18—an inversion of the work’s main theme—was so immediately popular that even the typically dour composer recognized its commercial appeal and commented, “This one’s for my agent.”

snippet.title: Seong-Jin Cho: Rachmaninoff’s Rhapsody on a Theme of Paganini, Op. 43 Var.18(20251203 Carnegie Hall)
snippet.description:
20251203 Carnegie Hall Presents Pittsburgh Symphony Orchestra
Stern Auditorium / Perelman Stage, Carnegie Hall, NY

Piano: Seong-Jin Cho
Pittsburgh Symphony Orchestra
Conductor : Manfred Honeck

Pianist Seong-Jin Cho joins the Pittsburgh Symphony Orchestra and conductor Manfred Honeck in a performance of Rachmaninoff’s Rhapsody on a Theme of Paganini. 

A virtuosic set of 24 variations inspired by the last of Niccolò Paganini’s 24 Caprices for Solo Violin, Rhapsody on a Theme of Paganini received its New York premiere at Carnegie Hall in 1934 with the composer as soloist alongside the New York Philharmonic led by Bruno Walter.

The swooning melody of Variation 18—an inversion of the work’s main theme—was so immediately popular that even the typically dour composer recognized its commercial appeal and commented, “This one’s for my agent.”

Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=j9IaApwieHg

snippet.title: Seong-Jin Cho: Rachmaninoff’s Rhapsody on a Theme of Paganini (Var.18) (20251203 Carnegie Hall)
snippet.description:
Pianist Seong-Jin Cho joins the Pittsburgh Symphony Orchestra and conductor Manfred Honeck in a performance of Rachmaninoff’s Rhapsody on a Theme of Paganini. 

A virtuosic set of 24 variations inspired by the last of Niccolò Paganini’s 24 Caprices for Solo Violin, Rhapsody on a Theme of Paganini received its New York premiere at Carnegie Hall in 1934 with the composer as soloist alongside the New York Philharmonic led by Bruno Walter.

The swooning melody of Variation 18—an inversion of the work’s main theme—was so immediately popular that even the typically dour composer recognized its commercial appeal and commented, “This one’s for my agent.”

20250826 Yannick Nézet-Séguin & SEONG-JIN CHO at the Lucerne Festival 2025
KKL Luzern, Lucerne, Switzerland

The Lucerne Festival Orchestra , Yannick Nézet-Séguin and Seong-Jin Cho  inspired their audience with wonderful performances of Beethoven's Piano Concerto No. 3 and Bruckner's "Romantic" Fourth Symphony.

The artists dedicated this concert to the memory of the late Alfred Brendel, who performed this exact concerto with the Lucerne Festival Orchestra and later was a mentor to Seong-Jin Cho.

Lucerne Festival Orchestra
Conductor : Yannick Nézet-Séguin

snippet.title: Seong-Jin Cho speaks about Ravel's solo piano works (20250111 Berlin)
snippet.description:
20250111 Seong-Jin Cho speaks about Ravel's solo piano works.
Siemens-Villa, Berlin, Germany

“I’ve always been fascinated by the ideas, colours and emotions to be found in Ravel’s music, and it has been an honour to record his complete solo piano works and concertos” (Seong-Jin Cho)

He has chosen to mark the 150th anniversary of the composer’s birth in 2025 by recording his complete solo piano music and the two piano concertos, where he collaborates with the Boston Symphony Orchestra and Andris Nelsons. 

Ten years on from his Chopin Competition victory, Cho released the first of the two albums, Ravel: The Complete Solo Piano Works, on 17 January 2025 (digitally and on two CDs).


* Broadcasted again online streaming from stage-plus.com on 5 Feb 2025.
  (before his Recital at Carnegie Hall )
* Broadcasted online streaming from stage-plus.com on 11 Jan 2025.
* Interviewed in Berlin’s beautiful Siemens-Villa on 9 Sep 2024.

snippet.title: 5 questions for Seong-Jin Cho : We ask, Cho plays his answers on the piano (20240928 Berlin)
snippet.description:
20240928  5 questions for Seong-Jin Cho: 
We ask, Cho plays his answers on the piano

As the winner of the legendary Chopin Competition and a “poet at the piano” (Simon Rattle), Seong-Jin Cho has made a name for himself internationally. He will now accompany the Berliner Philharmoniker as Artist in Residence through the 2024/25 season.
To kick off his residency, we asked Seong-Jin Cho five questions that he was only allowed to answer on the piano. For example: What is your earliest musical memory? Which piece do you play to warm up? In the end, our artist in residence did say a few words. 

Source: https://www.berliner-philharmoniker.de/en/concert/calendar/55629/
Video: Adam Janisch
